clue.text: Job maybe duplicating software for avid reader

parts.note: Job is one example of a book of the Bible
a worm is a computer program that copies itself across networks

explanation.surface: Someone at work keeps copying programs illegally to feed a reading habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like employment, but with its capital it is the Old Testament book, given by 'maybe' as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads constantly and greedily is affectionately called this, an idiom for a keen reader.

clue.text: Resentful person using tooth, covering its tip

indicators.note: covering means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: someone who bites is a biter
the tip of tooth is its first letter, T

explanation.surface: An aggrieved patient chewing with a tooth that is capped.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling aggrieved and resentful is being bitter, a synonym.

clue.text: Forest-dweller with red hair, almost bright ginger?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bright ginger is the colour orange

explanation.surface: A woodland creature with ginger fur, almost glowing.
explanation.walkthrough: ORANG is short for orang-utan, the red-haired ape of Borneo and Sumatra.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a red-haired ape living in rainforest, an example of the definition.

clue.text: What's the reason to sulk in speech? Utter defeat

indicators.note: in speech means the words are taken as spoken, sound not spelling

parts.note: the question asks why pout

explanation.surface: Asking why one should sulk, then admitting total defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question's words, why pout, said together give the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A total rout or crushing loss is a wipeout, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Check bank document putting one in one's place again

definitions.text: putting one in one's place again

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a bank statement lists account transactions

explanation.surface: Examining a bank statement to restore someone's position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in one's place' means restoring a person to their old job, not putting them down.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoring someone to a former position is their reinstatement, a noun of action.

clue.text: Really subtle skill required to eject leader

indicators.note: ejecting the leader means the first letter of the word for subtle skill is thrown out

parts.note: finesse is delicate skill or refinement

explanation.surface: Genuine delicacy of touch apparently needed to oust the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eject leader' removes F, the first letter of FINESSE. IN ESSE is Latin for 'in actual existence'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means existing in actuality, so it stands for really or actually.

clue.text: Label to identify sentry, perhaps heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a gateman guarding an entrance is a kind of sentry

explanation.surface: An identity badge for a guard on his way north.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge bearing one's name, worn to show who one is, is an identifying label.

clue.text: Pottery from unused area in shop

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for shop

parts.note: a store is a shop
something unused is new

explanation.surface: Ceramics found in a disused part of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense, hard fired clay ware is a type of pottery, so the answer is an example.

clue.text: Old king left inside chained up, losing the crown

indicators.note: inside means one letter sits within the other piece
losing the crown means the top letter is removed

parts.note: tethered means tied or chained up

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch is chained in a cell, stripped of his crown.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the crown is the first letter, so TETHERED loses T to give ETHERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred the Unready was an Anglo-Saxon king of England, an example.

clue.text: Stepping on very young person living rough, perhaps

parts.note: a tramp is a homeless person sleeping rough
the suffix -ling marks a young or small one, as in duckling

explanation.surface: Treading on a child who sleeps on the streets, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' admits the invented word: a young tramp would be a trampling, as a young duck is a duckling.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading heavily on something is trampling it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Clown appearing twice, the second time topless, receives sillier greeting

indicators.note: receives means the first clown takes the next word inside

parts.note: a goon is a clownish, foolish person
dafter means sillier

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a goon is a clownish, foolish person

explanation.surface: A clown turns up twice, the second time shirtless, and a sillier one says hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing twice, the second time' tells you GOON is used twice; the second copy loses G.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite salutation used after midday, an example of a greeting.

clue.text: Loiter without enthusiasm in Low Church

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Hanging about half-heartedly in an evangelical-free, plain style of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low Church' reads as the Anglican tradition, but 'Low' is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf about aimlessly and listlessly is to mooch, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Songs're arranged to be fascinating

indicators.note: songs that are arranged have their parts reordered, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Musical numbers are scored so as to grip an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb someone's whole attention is to grip or fascinate them, a synonym.

clue.text: Old cash machine with each pound showing greyish-yellow colour

parts.note: an ATM is an automated teller machine dispensing cash
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: An ancient cash dispenser paying out a pound each time looks dingy.
explanation.definitionFit: The pale greyish fawn of rolled oats gives its name to this colour shade.

clue.text: How poor Christian might begin meal, grudgingly

definitions.text: How poor Christian might begin meal
definitions.meaning: a Christian who says the blessing before eating badly would do it this way

explanation.surface: A badly-performed blessing before dinner done reluctantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 'grace' literally as the prayer before a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means doing something unwillingly and resentfully, so it matches reluctantly.

clue.text: Maid known to change her sex

indicators.note: changing the words alters their order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl who is known to be undergoing gender transition.
explanation.definitionFit: Women collectively form the female sex, so this word means her sex.

clue.text: Chinese dog rounding up pets roaming in Welsh town

indicators.note: rounding up means the dog encloses the next piece

parts.note: a chow is a dog breed from China

indicators.note: roaming means wandering, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A Chinese breed herding stray pets in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roaming' rearranges PETS to EPST, held by CHOW. Chepstow is a town in Monmouthshire on the Wye.
explanation.definitionFit: Chepstow is a Monmouthshire town on the English border, an example of a Welsh town.

clue.text: Stirring theme somehow capturing ultimate in abode

definitions.text: Stirring theme somehow capturing ultimate in abode

indicators.note: capturing means the shuffled letters hold the next piece within them
stirring mixes things up, so the letters of the following words are mixed
the ultimate in a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A rousing melody that somehow captures the essence of the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' rearranges the letters of 'theme' and 'somehow', and 'capturing' holds E, the last letter of 'abode', named by 'ultimate in'. The whole clue also describes the sentimental song.
explanation.definitionFit: The old sentimental song of that name is a stirring tune celebrating the dwelling one loves.

clue.text: Restrain bristling anger after son is promoted to the top

parts.note: raised hackles show bristling anger

explanation.surface: Holding back fury after a boy gets a promotion.

clue.text: Men supposing Antarctic surface is opening

if means supposing
Antarctica is covered in ice

explanation.surface: Explorers wondering whether the polar ice has a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole or aperture, especially in the body, is an orifice, a synonym for opening.

clue.text: Sticky catch on boundaries from googly?

parts.note: to catch on is to twig, to understand

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.definitionFit: Full of sticks or twigs is the literal sense, a crossword sense of sticky as having sticks.

clue.text: Criticise soap presentation and fall flat?

soap is often presented as a cake, a solid block

explanation.surface: Slating a television soap opera's showing and watching it flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soap' suggests a TV serial, but it is the washing bar sold in cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft that pancakes drops flat onto the ground, a figurative sense marked by the question mark.

clue.text: Water-colour production from painter using East End location?

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a stock abbreviation for a painter
Bow is a district of London's East End, so being there is being in Bow

explanation.surface: A watercolour painted by an artist working in the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is an area of the East End of London. 'Water-colour production' is witty: sunlight and rain produce a coloured arc.

clue.text: Developed, except round Israel's borders

clue.text: Crowded hospital beset by parasite

clue.text: Unfaithful couple essential for comedy?

clue.text: Tungsten I had to procure for gizmo

clue.text: A new call to preserve established line
